## Household and background

Kenji Nakamura (born November 2, 1990) and Amara Nakamura (born July 19, 1991) are married and file jointly. They own the house at 2140 Windrow Court and have two children: Sora (born March 15, 2019 — 6) and Theo (born August 4, 2022 — 3). Both children lived with them all year and neither provided any of their own support.

BOTH parents work, which is the pivot of this return. Kenji is a logistics planner at Halcyon Logistics Group (W-2 box 1 $62,480.00, box 2 $5,920.00); Amara is a branch librarian for the Birchwood Public Library System (W-2 box 1 $34,120.00, box 2 $2,460.00). No other income at all — no interest, no investments.

Both children attend Willow Grove Early Learning Center full time so that both parents can work: $11,800.00 paid to the centre in 2025 ($4,970.00 for Sora, $6,830.00 for Theo — infant care costs more). The centre's year-end statement gives its name, address and EIN, which Form 2441 requires; without them the credit is disallowed outright.

## Interview

**Q.** Did BOTH of you work during the year? The dependent-care credit needs earned income from each spouse.

**A.** Yes — Kenji full time, Amara four days a week at the library.

**Q.** Why did you pay for care? The rule is that it has to let you work or look for work.

**A.** Exactly that. Neither of us could work without it — we'd have to drop to one income.

**Q.** Did either employer offer a dependent-care FSA, and did you use it?

**A.** The library mentioned one but we never enrolled. Nothing came out pre-tax and there's no box 10 on either W-2.

**Q.** Is the centre a licensed provider, and do you have its EIN in writing?

**A.** Yes — it's on the year-end statement they gave us in January.

**Q.** Are both children under 13 for the whole year?

**A.** Sora is 6, Theo is 3. Yes.

**Q.** Did you claim this credit last year or carry anything forward?

**A.** No — Theo only started at the centre this year and we didn't claim it before.

**Q.** Has the IRS ever disallowed a credit for you?

**A.** No.

## Preparer notes

- Form 2441: $11,800 paid, but the credit is computed on $6,000 — the EXPENSE CAP is $3,000 if there is ONE qualifying person and $6,000 if there are TWO OR MORE (§21(c)); it is a household ceiling, not $3,000 per child (a third child would not raise it), and it is not per provider. The earned-income limit (the LOWER spouse's $34,120) does not bind. The applicable percentage is AGI-graded, 35% down to 20%, and at $96,600 of AGI it is floored at 20% → credit $1,200. An $11,800 bill buys a $1,200 credit; the interview should say so plainly rather than let the client expect more.
- CTC: both children under 17 with unrestricted SSNs (and so are both parents — the TY2025 filer-SSN requirement) → $4,400, all of it NONREFUNDABLE here because the $7,338 tax absorbs it. Nothing spills into the refundable ACTC (contrast profile-hoh-children, where the tax is small and most of the credit is refunded).
- Ordering matters: the dependent-care credit is taken before the child tax credit, so the CTC sees $7,338 − $1,200 = $6,138 of tax. Still more than $4,400, so both credits fit whole.
- AGI $96,600 is far above the EITC's $64,430 MFJ two-child ceiling — no EITC. Total tax $1,738; withholding $8,380 → refund $6,642.
